description: The shared Kryon conformance corpus. Every SDK runs these against its own implementation via the helper contract in spec/conformance.md. Cases are language-neutral by construction: they never reference echo, sleep or /bin/sh, because those differ across platforms and half of them do not exist on Windows.

cases.why: The single most basic promise Kryon makes. If this regresses, nothing else matters.
The security guarantee of the whole project: execute() never lets the shell see an argument. If this ever passes through a shell, every caller interpolating user input has a command-injection hole.
An empty argument is a real argument. Dropping it silently shifts every later positional argument, which is the kind of bug that corrupts data rather than crashing.
A non-zero exit is information, not an exception. grep exits 1 to mean 'no match'; raising here would make ordinary code wrong by default.
The ok flag must mean exactly 'exited on its own with status 0', with no other path setting it.
stderr must be captured separately from stdout. Merging them loses the distinction callers use to decide what to show a user.
Both pipes must be drained concurrently. An implementation that reads stdout to completion first deadlocks as soon as a process fills the stderr pipe buffer.
check=true is the opt-in strict mode. It must convert unsuccessful results into errors, and must carry the result along so the stderr is not lost.
check must not raise on success, and must return the same result the non-check path would.
Failing to start is an error, not a result. There is no exit code to report for a process that never existed, and a synthetic one would be a flag every caller forgets to check.

A bad working directory must be its own error, not reported as a missing executable — and must never silently fall back to the current directory, which would run the command somewhere the caller did not intend.
Malformed requests are rejected before any system call. Validation is cheaper than cleanup.
A negative timeout is a caller mistake. Treating it as 'no timeout' or 'immediate' both silently do the wrong thing.
The default must be inheritance. A child that cannot see PATH or HOME breaks in ways that look like the program is broken.
env merges over the inherited environment rather than replacing it — the common case is adding one variable, not rebuilding the world.
Removing a variable must be expressible. Without it, there is no way to stop a secret in the parent environment reaching the child.
clear_env plus env is the environment allowlist, and it is the primary mechanism for keeping credentials out of a child process.
The allowlist must actually pass through what it allows.
Running a command in the wrong directory is a silent data-corruption bug, not a crash.
stdin must be written and then closed. A child reading until end-of-input hangs forever if stdin is left open.
With no stdin supplied, stdin must still be closed rather than inherited or left open — otherwise every `cat`-like process hangs until the timeout.
A timeout that does not fire is worse than no timeout: the caller believed they were protected.
Output collected before the kill is the only evidence of what the process was doing. Discarding it makes timeouts undebuggable.
check must map each termination reason to its own error, so callers can retry a timeout without retrying a genuine failure.
SIGTERM is a request. A process that ignores it must still be killed after the grace period, or the timeout is a suggestion and the caller is blocked forever.
The point of an output cap is bounded memory. An implementation that buffers everything and truncates at the end has not enforced anything.
A cap that is not reached must be invisible — no truncation flag, no altered termination.
Hitting a resource limit is distinguishable from failing, so a caller can raise the limit rather than debug the command.
Terminal output is not ASCII. Multi-byte characters, combining marks and astral-plane emoji must survive the round trip intact.
Without an explicit encoding, output is bytes. Guessing a codec is how mojibake gets baked into logs.
Escape sequences must reach the caller untouched. Kryon captures terminal output; interpreting it is the emulator's job, and stripping it would make that impossible.
execute_shell must actually reach a shell, otherwise its separate existence is a lie and callers will reach for something worse.
The whole reason spawn exists is that output arrives while the process runs. If chunks only appear at exit, this is execute with extra steps.
Interactive use is write-then-read repeatedly. A write that is buffered until close makes every REPL-style session hang.
A process the caller asked to stop must actually be gone, on every platform, including the one with no SIGTERM.
Leaving the block must kill the process. A leaked child outlives the program that created it and nobody notices until a machine runs out of process slots.
